channel.title: Settings on Termorq
channel.description: Recent content in Settings on Termorq

item.title: Preferences
item.description:
Open Settings with Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS), from the jump list, or by selecting the avatar. The cursor starts in the search box. The page groups preferences into Application, Workspace, Appearance, Terminal, (in Pro) AI, and Record.

Search settings, under the page title, filters the page as you type. A setting stays when its name, help text, or a field hint holds every word you type, in any order. A group whose title matches keeps all its settings. Groups with no match, and their links on the left, are hidden, and the matching words are highlighted. Esc clears the search; with the box empty, Esc closes Settings.

item.title: Forges
item.description:
Settings → Forges connects Termorq to GitHub (github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server), GitLab (gitlab.com or a self-managed instance) or Azure DevOps (an organisation and, optionally, a project). Type @create forge at the prompt to open the same form, or search Settings for “forge”, “gitlab” or “token”.

  1. Pick the provider card.
  2. Leave Base URL blank for the cloud host, or enter your server, for example https://git.example.com. For Azure DevOps, type the organisation or paste a https://dev.azure.com/contoso/Project URL into Organisation.
  3. Paste a token. The form lists the scopes it needs:
    • GitHub: repo (read) and notifications on a classic token. That repo scope covers the private repositories the account can open. A fine-grained token covers only the repositories selected on it. See Private repositories.
    • GitLab: read_api.
    • Azure DevOps: Code (Read), Build (Read) and Work Items (Read).
  4. Select Test connection. It shows Connected as your login, or what is wrong, such as a missing scope.
  5. Select Save forge. A new connection saves only after a passing test.

item.title: Todos and watchers
item.description:
Watchers are saved checks on your forge connections. While Termorq is open, each forge is checked in the background on its own schedule, and anything new lands in Todos: review requests, approvals you are required for, pull requests waiting on you, failed or finished pipelines on your branches, and work assigned to you.

  • GitHub: notifications, review requests and Actions runs. A private repository is included when the token can read it. See Private repositories.
  • GitLab: To-Do items and pipelines.
  • Azure DevOps: pull requests where you are a reviewer or a required approver, and pipeline runs.

Open Todos with the 🔔 Todos button in the title bar (it shows the unread count), Ctrl+Shift+O (Cmd+Shift+O on macOS), Todos in the rail or the Ctrl+J jump list, or @todo at the prompt.

item.title: CI status, logs and re-run
item.description: When the current tab’s folder is a clone of a repository on one of your forge connections, the status strip shows a CI chip for the branch you are on: GitHub Actions runs, GitLab pipelines or Azure DevOps builds. It works on any branch, not only the ones your watchers cover.

item.title: Start work from a ticket
item.description: From @work, pick an issue or work item you want to work on and press Start work. Termorq suggests a branch name, finds your local clone, and shows the exact git commands before it runs anything. It always branches from the remote’s default branch, never from your local main.

item.title: Free and Pro feature comparison
item.description:
Termorq has Free and Pro editions. This table shows which features each edition includes. The edition is the FREE or PRO pill at the right of the header. Free also shows created by Garrard Kitchen on the footer. Open License from the jump list (Ctrl+J) to compare plans; the current build is highlighted.

The root features.yml manifest is the source of this feature list and the app’s feature availability. Every new feature must have an explicit plan assignment there.
